finding.claim: Balance check and debit are not atomic, so concurrent requests can overdraw an account.
finding.source: Concurrent POST /transfer (bank.py:7-8) or POST /withdraw (bank.py:18-19) for the same account
finding.sink: Debit at bank.py:13 and bank.py:23 against module-level BAL dict

trace.note: balance read and compared to amount
separate debit statement, no lock held across check and debit

finding.guards_checked: No lock, transaction, or atomic operation. BAL is a shared global dict; threaded server serves requests concurrently. Race window is narrow and timing-dependent (moderate confidence).

verdict.guard_found: none. No lock, transaction, or atomic operation guards the check-then-debit at bank.py:11-13 (/transfer) or bank.py:21-23 (/withdraw). BAL is a plain module-level dict (bank.py:4). The only checks are the balance comparisons themselves, which are not atomic with the debit.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: the balance is compared at bank.py:11 and debited at bank.py:13, and the same pattern appears at bank.py:21 and bank.py:23, with no lock between check and debit. An authenticated account holder (g.user, set outside this file) can send concurrent /withdraw or /transfer requests, and because the server is threaded, two requests can both pass the check before either debit runs, overdrawing the account. The window is narrow, so exploitability is timing-dependent, but no effective control blocks it.
